print_errors.note: The preposition is printed with a dotted final ي (إلي) here, while إلى elsewhere on the page has no dots. Kept as printed.

notes: p069: p068 ends with a complete sentence «(ثلاثًا).» and has no footnotes, so the marker has no + and there is no (تابع). The An-Nas reference uses European digits: it looks like «6-1» in print and is written in reading order as [الناس: 1-6], the same way as the p068 example in CONVENTIONS. The space between ] and «(ثلاثًا)» matches keyB b17 (in print the ] touches the parenthesis). In the Fatiha, the basmala is printed in full size inside ﴿ as ayah (١), so it is written inside the brackets. The ﴾ and [ of the Saffat reference touch in print and the colons in «[الفاتحة:١-٧]» and «[طه:١١١]» are set tight; all three are written with the usual spacing «﴾ [سورة: n]». The bold-looking digits ٣٣ and (٢٠) are the normal heavy Arabic-Indic digits of the body font, not bold markup. p070: continues p069 («آيات الذكر / الحكيم») so it is marked +; footnote (١) has no final period in print. p071: the heading is printed as «الوظيفةالزروقيَّة» with no visible space; it is written per the STRUCTURE heading map. «المسماة بـ (سفينة …)» is printed with a tatweel after ب; the tatweel is dropped per §2, which leaves «ب (سفينة». In «أَعُوذُ بِاللهِ» only the printed kasra is written on the Allah ligature, as in keyB b14. Ayat al-Kursi runs from p071 onto p072 within one paragraph (p072 marked +). The print has no bracket at the page break, but validate.py needs ﴿﴾ balanced on each line, so ﴾ was added after «يَعْلَمُ» at the end of p071 and ﴿ before «مَا بَيْنَ» at the start of p072. A merge should remove these two brackets when the pages are joined. Waqf signs that Tanzil has at the end of the quoted fragments (16:53 ۖ, 2:255 ۚ after ٱلْقَيُّومُ on p071, 20:111 ۖ) are not printed and were not added. Every Quran span was checked word by word against the zoomed print. scripts/quran.py reports no other differences from Tanzil.
